They answered him, “We don’t know.” Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things.”
“But what do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first and said to him, ‘My son, go and work in the vineyard today.’
He answered, ‘I do not want to.’ But afterward he changed his mind and went.
He went to the other and said the same thing to him. He answered, ‘I will, sir,’ but did not go.
Which of these two did his father’s will?” They said to him, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, tax collectors and prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Even after you saw this, you did not change your minds afterward and believe him.
Listen to another parable. There was a landowner who planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower in it. He leased it to farmers and went away on a journey.
When the harvest season arrived, he sent his servants to the farmers so that they would send him some of the fruit of his vineyard.
The farmers seized his servants; some they beat, some they stoned, and some they killed.
Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
Finally he sent his son to them, saying, ‘Perhaps they will respect my son.’
But when the farmers saw the son, they said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
And they seized him, took him outside the vineyard, and killed him.
So when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?
They said to him, “He will utterly destroy those wicked men and lease the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruit at the proper times.”
Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in Scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This has come from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?
“Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who produce fruit.
“Whoever falls on this stone will be shattered, and anyone it falls on will be crushed.”
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he was speaking about them.
They wanted to arrest him, but they were afraid of the crowd, because the people regarded him as a prophet.
Jesus spoke again in parables and said:
“The kingdom of heaven is like a king who held a wedding feast for his son.
“He sent his servants to summon those invited to the wedding feast, but they were unwilling to come.
“Again he sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell those invited: Look, my meal is ready. My oxen and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.’
“But they disregarded it and went away, one to his farm and another to his business.
“The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
“When the king heard, he became angry and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
“Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.
“‘So go to the places where the roads lead out, and invite everyone you find to the wedding feast.’
“Those servants went out onto the roads and gathered everyone they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests reclining at the meal.
“The king came in to see the guests and saw a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.
“He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But he remained silent.
“Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind his hands and feet and take him out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.’
“For many are called, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and plotted how to trap him in something he said.

They sent their disciples to him along with the supporters of Herod, saying to him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God truthfully. You are not concerned about anyone’s opinion, for you do not show favoritism.
“So tell us what you think: Is it lawful to pay the poll tax to Caesar or not?”
But Jesus knew their wickedness and said, “Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?”
“Show me the denarius used for the poll tax.” They brought him a denarius.
Jesus said to them, “Whose image and inscription are these?”
They said, “Caesar’s.” He said to them, “Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and God what belongs to God.”
When they heard this, they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
That day Sadducees approached and said to him, “There is no resurrection of the dead.” And they questioned him,
saying to him, “Teacher, Moses told us that if a man dies without children, his brother should marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married a woman and died, and because he had no children, he left his wife to his brother.
The same happened to the second and the third, and so on through all seven.
Last of all, the woman also died.
At the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of these seven? For they all married her.”
Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
For at the resurrection of the dead, men do not marry women, nor do women become wives of men, but they are like the angels of God in heaven.
“But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read what God said to you when he said,”
‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob.’ And God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
One of them, who was an expert in the law, asked him a question to test him:
“Teacher, which commandment is greatest in the law?”
Jesus said to him, “Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind.
This is the greatest and first commandment.
And the second is like it: Love your neighbor as yourself.
On these two commandments hang the Law and the Prophets.”
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
saying, “What do you think about the Messiah? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “David’s son.”
He said to them, “How then does David, speaking by the Spirit, call him Lord? For he says,
“For the Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet.’”
“If David calls him Lord, then how is he his son?”
No one could give him an answer, and from that day on no one dared to question him again.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples,
and said to them, “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.
Therefore, observe and do everything they tell you to observe. But do not do as they do, for they say things but do not do them.
They tie up heavy burdens and put them on people’s shoulders, but they themselves are unwilling to touch them with a finger.
They do everything to be seen by people. They make their prayer boxes broad and lengthen the blue tassels on their cloaks.
They love the places of honor at dinners and the chief seats in the synagogues,
and greetings in the marketplaces, and being called ‘Rabbi’ by people.
But you must not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one teacher, and you are all brothers.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
And you must not be called leaders, because you have one leader, the Messiah.
The greatest among you must be your servant.
For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You devour widows’ houses while making long prayers as a pretense. Because of this, you will receive a more severe judgment.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in people’s faces. You do not enter yourselves, and you do not allow those who are entering to go in.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You travel over sea and land to make one convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If someone swears by the temple, it means nothing, but if someone swears by the gold in the temple, he is bound by his oath.’
You blind fools! For which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy?
And you say, ‘If someone swears by the altar, it means nothing, but if someone swears by the offering on it, he is bound by his oath.’
You blind fools! Which is greater: the offering, or the altar that makes the offering holy?
Therefore, whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.
And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who lives in it.
And whoever swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the one who sits on it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You give a tenth of your mint, dill, and cumin, but you have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You ought to have practiced these without neglecting the others.
You blind guides! You strain out gnats and swallow camels.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of plunder and wrongdoing.
Blind Pharisees, first clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that their outside may also be clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but inside are full of dead people's bones and every kind of uncleanness.
In the same way, you outwardly appear righteous to people, but inside you are full of wickedness and hypocrisy.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! You build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the burial places of the righteous.
And you say, “If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets.”
So you testify against yourselves that you are the descendants of those who killed the prophets.
You too, then, fill up the measure of your ancestors!
Snakes, offspring of vipers! How will you escape being condemned to hell?
Therefore, look, I am sending you prophets, wise people, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and some you will flog in your synagogues and pursue from city to city.

Thus all the blood of the righteous that has been shed on earth will come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
Look, your house is left to you desolate.
For I tell you, you will not see me from now on until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'
Jesus left the temple to go away, and his disciples came up and pointed out the temple building to him.
But he said to them, 'Do you not see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left upon another that will not be torn down.'
As Jesus sat on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came up and spoke to him privately: 'Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the world?'
Jesus answered them, 'Be careful that no one leads you astray.'
For many will come in my name and say, 'I am the Messiah,' and they will lead many astray.
You will hear of wars and reports of battles. See that you are not alarmed, for all these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.
But all these things are the beginning of the birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to suffering and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.
Then many will fall away, hate one another, and betray one another.
Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
Because wickedness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
But when you see the defiling sign of desolation spoken of by Daniel the prophet standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
Then those who are in Judea should flee to the mountains.
and whoever is on the roof must not go down to take what is in his house.
And whoever is in the field must not turn back to take his clothing.
But how terrible it will be for pregnant women and those nursing children in those days!
Pray that your escape will not be in winter or on the Sabbath.
For then there will be great suffering, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the world until now, and never will again.
And if those days had not been shortened, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, the Messiah is here!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.
For false messiahs and lying prophets will arise and perform great signs so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Look, I have told you beforehand.
So if they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness!’ do not go out; or ‘Look, he is in the inner room!’ do not believe it.
For just as lightning comes from the east and is visible as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.
Immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will grow dark, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
And he will send his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
Now learn the lesson from the fig tree: as soon as its branches become tender and its leaves sprout, you know that summer has arrived.
So you too, when you see all these things, know that it has reached the door.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day and that hour, not even the angels of heaven, but only the Father.
As it was in the days of Noah, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For before the flood they were eating and drinking, taking wives and giving women in marriage to men, until the day Noah entered the ark.
And they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away. So will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Then two will be in the village; one will be taken and one will be left.
And two women will be grinding at a mill; one will be taken and one will be left.
Therefore stay awake, because you do not know at what hour your Lord is coming.
But know this: if the owner of the house had known during which watch of the night the thief would come, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Therefore, you too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.
Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom his master has put in charge of his household to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing this when he comes.
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of everything he owns.
But if that wicked servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’
and begins to beat his fellow servants and eats and drinks with drunkards,
that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know.
He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
Five of them were wise, and five were foolish.
The foolish ones took their lamps but took no oil with them.
But the wise ones took oil in containers along with their lamps.
But when the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
At midnight there was a shout: ‘Look, the bridegroom is coming! Go out to meet him!’
Then all those virgins got up and put their lamps in order.
The foolish ones said to the wise ones, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps have gone out.’
The wise ones answered, ‘There may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves.’
While they were away buying it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Later the other virgins also came and said, ‘Our lord, our lord, open the door for us!’
But he answered them, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’
Therefore, stay awake, because you do not know that day or the hour.
For it is like a man who set out on a journey: he called his servants and entrusted his possessions to them.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, each according to his ability. Then he immediately set out on his journey.
The one who had received five talents went and traded with them and gained five more.
Likewise, the one with two earned two more.
But the one who received one went and dug in the ground and hid his master's money.
After a long time, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received five talents came forward and brought five more. He said, "Master, you gave me five talents. Look, I have earned five more with them."
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a little; I will put you in charge of much. Enter into your master's joy."
The one with two talents came forward and said, "Master, you gave me two talents. Look, I have earned two more with them."
His master said to him, "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a little; I will put you in charge of much. Enter into your master's joy."
Then the one who had received one talent also came forward and said, "Master, I knew you were a harsh man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter seed.
I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what belongs to you."
His master answered him, “You wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter.”
"You should have deposited my money with the bankers, and when I came, I would have recovered what was mine with its interest.
So take the talent away from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
And throw the useless servant out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there."
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, with all his holy angels, then he will sit on his glorious throne.
All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
Then the king will say to those on his right, "Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me a drink; I was a stranger, and you took me in.
I was naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me."
Then the righteous will say to him, "Our Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?
When did we see you as a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?"
The king will answer them, "Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of mine, you did for me."
Then he will also say to those on his left, "Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat; I was thirsty and you gave me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger and you did not take me in; I was naked and you did not clothe me; I was sick and in prison and you did not visit me.
Then they too will answer, “Our Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and not serve you?”
Then he will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of these little ones, you did not do for me either.’
And these will go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life.
And when Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
“You know that in two days it will be Passover, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
They plotted to arrest Jesus by deceit and kill him.
But they were saying, ‘Not during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.’
When Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman approached him carrying a flask of very expensive perfumed oil, and she poured it over Jesus’ head as he reclined at the table.
When his disciples saw this, they were indignant and said, ‘Why this waste?
For this could have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor.’
But Jesus knew and said to them, ‘Why are you troubling the woman? She has done a good deed for me.
For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.
By pouring this perfume on my body, she has done it to prepare me for burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this good news of mine is proclaimed throughout the world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her.’
Then one of the Twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said to them, ‘What are you willing to give me if I hand him over to you?’ They agreed to give him thirty pieces of silver.
From then on he looked for an opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and said to him, ‘Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?’
He said to them, ‘Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, “Our teacher says: My time has come. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’
His disciples did as Jesus had instructed them and prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, he was reclining at the table with his twelve disciples.
As they were eating, he said, ‘Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.’
They were deeply distressed and began to say to him, one by one, ‘Surely it is not I, my Lord?’
He answered, ‘The one who dips his hand into the dish with me will betray me.’
And the Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
Judas, the betrayer, said in reply, ‘Surely it is not I, Rabbi?’ Jesus said to him, ‘You have said it.’
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, ‘Take, eat; this is my body.’
He took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Take it; drink from it, all of you.”
“This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.”
“But I tell you that from now on I will not drink from this fruit of the vine until the day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”
They sang praises and went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will fall away because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of his flock will be scattered.’”
But after I rise, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.
Peter answered him, “Even if everyone falls away because of you, I will never fall away because of you.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
Peter said to him, “Even if I have to die with you, I will not deny you.” And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane and said to his disciples, “Sit here while I go and pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him and began to be sorrowful and distressed.
And he said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here for me and keep watch with me.”
He went a little farther, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I want, but as you want.”
He came to his disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “So, could you not stay awake with me for one hour?”
“Stay awake and pray so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
Again he went away a second time and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.”
And he came again and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
He left them and went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to his disciples and said to them, “Sleep now and rest. Look, the hour has arrived, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.”
“Get up, let us go. Look, the one who betrays me has arrived.”
While he was still speaking, Judas the betrayer, one of the Twelve, arrived. With him was a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
Judas the betrayer had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him.”
And immediately he approached Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
But Jesus said to him, “Is this what you came for, my friend?” Then they approached, laid their hands on Jesus, and seized him.
And one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, “Put the sword back in its place, for all who take up swords will die by swords.”
“Or do you think I cannot ask my Father, and he will provide me right now with more than twelve legions of angels?”
“How, then, would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say that it must happen this way?”
At that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me as though I were a bandit? Every day I sat with you in the temple and taught, and you did not arrest me.”
But this happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled. Then all the disciples deserted him and fled.
Those who had arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Simon Peter followed him at a distance as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
The chief priests, the elders, and the whole council were looking for witnesses against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
But they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. Finally, two came forward
and said, “This man said, ‘I can tear down the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What is this testimony these men are giving against you?”
But Jesus remained silent. The high priest spoke and said to him, “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Messiah, the Son of God.”
Jesus said to him, “You have said it. But I tell you all that from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “Look, he has blasphemed! Why do we need witnesses anymore? You have now heard his blasphemy!
What do you want?” They answered, “He deserves death.”
Then they spat in his face and beat him with their fists, while others struck him.
And they said, “Prophesy to us, Messiah! Who was it that struck you?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
But he denied it before them all, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.”
When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to those who were there, “This man too was with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Again he denied it with oaths: “I do not know the man.”
A little later, those standing there came up and said to Peter, “You certainly are one of them, for even your speech gives you away.”
Then he began to curse and swear, “I do not know the man.” At that very moment a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
They bound him, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that Jesus had been condemned. He felt remorse and went and returned those thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and the elders.
He said, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.” But they said to him, “What is that to us? That is your concern.”
He threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver and said, “It is not lawful to put it into the temple treasury, because it is blood money.”
They took counsel and used it to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
For this reason that field has been called the Village of Blood to this day.
Then what had been spoken through the prophet was fulfilled: “I took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the valued one, whose price the Israelites had set,
and I gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me.”
Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You have said it.”
While the chief priests and elders were accusing him, he gave no answer.
Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how much they are testifying against you?”
He gave him no answer, not even a single word, and he was greatly amazed at this.
At every festival, the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner to the people, whichever one they wanted.
They had a well-known prisoner in custody called Barabbas.
When they had gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you, Barabbas or Jesus who is called the Messiah?”
For Pilate knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
While the governor was sitting on his judgment seat, his wife sent him a message, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered greatly today in my dream because of him.”
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.
The governor said to them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”
Pilate said to them, “And what shall I do with Jesus who is called the Messiah?” They all said, “Let him be crucified!”
The governor said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they shouted all the louder, saying, “Let him be crucified!”

When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that the uproar was only growing, he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this righteous man's blood. See to it yourselves.”
All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children.”
Then he released Barabbas to them, had Jesus flogged with whips, and handed him over to be crucified.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus into the governor's headquarters and gathered the whole cohort around him.
They stripped him and dressed him in a scarlet cloak.
They wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and placed a reed in his right hand. They knelt before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spat in his face, took the reed, and kept striking him on the head.
After they had mocked him, they took the cloak off him, dressed him in his own clothes, and led him away to be crucified.
And as they went out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry his cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which means “Skull.”
They gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink. He tasted it but would not drink it.
And when they had crucified him, they divided his clothes by casting lots.
They sat there and kept watch over him.
Above his head they placed the charge for which he was put to death, in writing: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
And two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads
and saying, “You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests also mocked him, along with the scribes, elders, and Pharisees,
saying, “He saved others, but he cannot save himself! If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
He trusts in God; let God rescue him now, if he delights in him. For he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
Likewise, the robbers who were crucified with him also taunted him.
Now from the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
About the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
But some of those standing there, when they heard it, said, “This man is calling Elijah.”
Immediately, one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
But the others said, “Leave him alone! Let us see whether Elijah comes to rescue him.”
But Jesus cried out again in a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
Immediately, the front of the temple entrance was split in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.
The tombs were opened, and many bodies of holy people who had fallen asleep were raised.
And they came out, and after his resurrection they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were terrified and said, “Truly, this man was the Son of God!”
Many women were also there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and had served him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too had become a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate ordered that the body be given to him.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen sheet.
He laid it in his own new tomb, which was cut into the rock. They rolled a large stone into place against the entrance of the tomb and went away.
Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
The next day, the day after Friday, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate
and said to him, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was still alive, he said, ‘After three days I will rise.’

So order the tomb to be guarded until the third day, so that his disciples do not come at night, steal him, and tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’ Then the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “You have guards. Go and secure it as best you know how.”
So they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone and posting guards.
On the evening of the Sabbath, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, approached, rolled the stone away from the entrance, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
The guards trembled with fear of him and became like dead men.
But the angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid, for I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
He is not here, for he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where our Lord was laid.
Go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead. Look, he is going ahead of you to Galilee; you will see him there. Now I have told you.”
They left the tomb quickly with fear and great joy and ran to tell his disciples.
And Jesus met them and said to them, “Peace to you!” They approached, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and they will see me there.”
While they were on their way, some of those guards came into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
They gathered with the elders, took counsel, and gave a large sum of money to the guards,
telling them, “Say, ‘His disciples came at night and stole him while we were asleep.’
And if the governor hears about this, we will persuade him and keep you free from worry.”
So they took the money and did as they had been instructed. And this story has circulated among the Jews to this day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had arranged to meet them.
When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some of them doubted.
Jesus approached and spoke with them, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. And just as my Father sent me, I am sending you.
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, and baptize them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Teach them to keep everything I have commanded you. And look, I am with you every day until the end of the world. Amen.”
